item.title: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman pushes for more RAM amid AI‑driven shortages
item.description:
OpenAI CEO Sam Altman pushes for more RAM amid AI‑driven shortages

OpenAI chief Sam Altman has taken to X to argue that everyone should be able to install as much memory as they want in their computers, even as AI data centers are depleting the global DRAM supply.

🔍 Overview

Altman’s comments came after an interview on the Cheeky Pint podcast where he described the situation as “quite terrible to have everybody have a bunch of the world’s limited supply of DRAM sitting in their own computer and being used five percent of the time.”

🗣️ Altman’s public statements

  • Changed his X handle to “Ram Altman” in response to a user comment.
  • Stated, “i actually do want the world to have tons of memory and people to put as much as they want in their computers… i have been arguing for the world to ramp up memory production for a long time.”
  • Repeated on X, “i want you to have so much ram” and “let’s build more.”
  • Emphasised that people should be free to “put as much as they want in their computers.”

📉 Drivers of the RAM shortage

  • AI data centers are aggressively buying the world’s RAM, creating price hikes and limiting availability for ordinary consumers.
  • The shortage is reinforced by the fact that much of the installed DRAM is under‑utilized, according to Altman’s podcast remarks.

📅 Outlook

  • Intel expects the RAM shortage to persist through at least next year.
  • SK Hynix predicts the shortage could drag on until 2030.
Company Forecast
Intel Shortage expected through at least next year
SK Hynix Shortage could drag on until 2030

Altman’s stance highlights a tension between the growing memory needs of AI workloads and the limited global DRAM supply.

#OpenAI #RAMshortage #AIInfrastructure #SamAltman

Source: Sam Altman addresses RAM comments: people should ‘put as much as they want in their computers’

item.title: Steam review backlog grows as AI-generated game content slows approvals
item.description:
Steam review backlog grows as AI-generated game content slows approvals

Indie developers are reporting unusually long wait times for Steam store and page approvals, causing missed launch dates.

🔍 Overview

Steam’s game‑store review process is currently behind schedule, with some developers waiting weeks for final approval. The delay is affecting indie launch plans.

📈 Reported Delays

  • Studio Daimon’s Food Devils was scheduled for early‑access launch on the day of submission (Oct 12) but is still “awaiting approval” according to director Alfred Kamon.
  • 2 Left Thumbs missed the planned launch of Wheel Make It by nearly two weeks because of a long build‑review wait.
  • One developer has been waiting for weeks on approval for a game it planned to release today.
  • Multiple other recent social‑media posts describe similar build‑review wait times.

⏳ Expected Review Times vs. Reality

  • Valve’s developer site states a typical review takes 3‑5 business days, and recommends submitting at least 7 business days before the desired live date.
  • In a new post, Valve acknowledges a “significant increase in submissions for store and page review” and says reviews are now taking up to 12 business days.

🤖 AI “slop” Impact

  • Kamon and 2 Left Thumbs suspect the longer waits are due to “slop” slowing down the process and say, “We can only assume it’s because Steam’s review queue is clogged up by AI slop, but the whole process is now taking several weeks for some developers.”
  • Valve notes that much of the delay is “having to re‑review games,” implying additional scrutiny of AI‑related content.
  • A Reddit analysis found 49.9 % of games released since Valve began requiring AI disclosure in 2024 now include an AI disclosure.

🚧 Platform Responses

  • Valve has updated its release checklist, now requiring developers to run a game on Steam for at least five minutes, and says further improvements to the build‑review process are forthcoming.
  • Itch.io reports a doubling of daily game‑page creations over the past two months and recently “deleted a couple terabytes of ai slop.”

📊 Summary of Affected Developers

Developer / Studio Game Planned Launch Reported Delay
Studio Daimon Food Devils (early‑access) Oct 12 (submission) – launch today Still awaiting approval; weeks of wait
2 Left Thumbs Wheel Make It Launch missed by ~2 weeks Long build‑review wait
Unnamed developer – Launch today Weeks of wait

These facts illustrate a growing bottleneck in Steam’s approval pipeline, linked to the surge in AI‑generated game content.

#Steam #GameDev #AIContent #IndieGames

Source: Indie games are missing launch dates because Steam is backed up

item.title: OpenAI Announces Navier‑Stokes Solution and Forms Advisory Panel Amid Backlash
item.description:
OpenAI Announces Navier‑Stokes Solution and Forms Advisory Panel Amid Backlash

OpenAI announced that its internal AI model has produced a solution to the Navier‑Stokes Millennium Prize problem, and the company responded to the ensuing controversy by creating an independent advisory panel of elite mathematicians.

🔍 Overview

  • OpenAI claimed one of its biggest prizes yet: a solution to a legendary Millennium Prize problem – the Navier‑Stokes problem, a challenge unsolved for around 90 years.
  • The breakthrough was presented in a blog post on a Tuesday and described as an achievement that demonstrates how quickly AI is transforming mathematics.
  • The announcement sparked immediate backlash from the mathematical community, raising concerns about academic norms, credit, and the motivations behind the work.

⚙️ What OpenAI announced

  • The solution was generated by an internal AI model that the company said is “more powerful than the newly re…”.
  • OpenAI framed the result as a historic achievement, noting that such a discovery would normally be celebrated.

📣 Community reaction

  • Mathematicians voiced unease, describing OpenAI as an “impossibly well‑resourced interloper” that appears to be driven by winning rather than advancing the field.
  • Accusations surfaced of scooping, spying, and violating long‑standing academic norms, which some fear could have a chilling effect on research.
  • Andreas Thom raised concerns that prior interactions with the ChatGPT chatbot may have contributed to the success, and OpenAI acknowledged that the result built heavily on his and Gábor Kun’s earlier work.
  • A second mathematician accused OpenAI of “unethical and dishonest” behavior and a lack of transparency about the origins of its training data.
  • Abhishek Saha, a mathematics professor at Queen Mary University of London, explained that OpenAI has engaged in “the kind of things that mathematicians will generally not do.”

🤝 OpenAI’s response

  • OpenAI announced a new independent panel of elite mathematicians tasked with advising the company and other AI firms on how to interact with mathematical research and the wider community.
  • The panel’s formation “caught many mathematicians by surprise,” and researchers questioned what the group will actually do, how much influence it will have, and whether OpenAI will heed its advice.
  • The first assignment for the panel is to help coordinate the release of scores of additional results that OpenAI says its unreleased model has produced, a prospect that has already stirred dread among researchers.

📈 Why it matters

  • The episode illustrates the tension between rapid AI‑driven discoveries and established scholarly practices.
  • How OpenAI manages the release of AI‑generated mathematics could shape future collaborations—or conflicts—between industry and the academic community.

#OpenAI #Mathematics #AIResearch #MillenniumPrize

Source: All the drama around AI’s takeover of mathematics

item.title: President Trump Calls Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang During All-In Summit
item.description:
President Trump Calls Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang During All-In Summit

Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang received a phone call from President Trump while onstage at the All-In Podcast’s All-In Summit on Monday. Huang placed the president on speakerphone to address the live audience.

🔍 Overview

During the live call, President Trump addressed concerns regarding the future of artificial intelligence. He described recent fears about AI development as a “hoax” and stated that “the robots will not be taking over.”

⚙️ Key details

  • President Trump’s comments followed an essay by Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei, which advocated for slowing AI development and increasing government coordination.
  • In response to the discourse, President Trump stated that he intends to push back against the current narrative surrounding AI risks.
  • The president also remarked on the economic impact of data centers, claiming they have turned struggling communities into wealthy ones.

💡 Why it matters

Following the president’s statements, Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang commented on the future of the industry:

Participant Stance on AI Future
President Trump The robots will not be taking over
Jensen Huang We’re going to make sure that everybody wins in the AI race in America

Huang further stated that he intends for every industry, company, state, and individual to benefit from the AI race in America.

#Nvidia #AI #JensenHuang #TechPolicy #AllInSummit

Source: Jensen Huang puts Trump on speakerphone onstage to announce robots won’t take over the world
